overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the minutes were accurate, unnoticed topics were not reasonably anticipated 48 hours ahead, and listing a topic under 'New Business' was permissible.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 18, 2012 minutes omitted a decision to send a letter to a property owner and did not accurately summarize discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law because its minutes are accurate.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee discussed topics not listed in the notice, including a plaque, a liaison report, and a citizen's forum.
allegations.key_passage: We conclude that these topics were not anticipated 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a presentation was listed under 'New Business' when it should have been listed under 'Old Business' in the meeting notice.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the topic was listed in the meeting notice with sufficient specificity, thus the public was aware the item would be discussed.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
